import cyclopts

app = cyclopts.App(
    name="mycli",
    config=cyclopts.config.Toml(
        "pyproject.toml",
        root_keys=("tool", "mycli"),
        search_parents=True,
        must_exist=False,
        use_commands_as_keys=False,
    ),
)


@app.command
def run(
    name: str = "world",
    *,
    count: int = 1,
    verbose: bool = False,
    output: Optional[Path] = None,
):
    """Greet someone, optionally multiple times.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name: Who to greet.
    count: Number of times to repeat the greeting.
    verbose: Print extra diagnostic information.
    output: Optional file to write the greeting to instead of stdout.
    """
    if verbose:
        print(f"[verbose] name={name!r} count={count} output={output}")

    lines = [f"Hello, {name}!" for _ in range(count)]
    text = "\n".join(lines)

    if output is not None:
        output.write_text(text + "\n")
        if verbose:
            print(f"[verbose] wrote {len(lines)} line(s) to {output}")
    else:
        print(text)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    app()

### Combine TOML and Environment Variable Configuration

Source: https://github.com/brianpugh/cyclopts/blob/main/docs/source/config_file.rst

Configure an application to use multiple config sources by passing a sequence to App.config. Environment variables take precedence over TOML settings.

```python
# character-counter.py
import cyclopts
from pathlib import Path

app = cyclopts.App(
    name="character-counter",
    config=[
        # Since Env comes before Toml, it has priority.
        cyclopts.config.Env("CHAR_COUNTER_"),
        cyclopts.config.Toml(
            "pyproject.toml",
            root_keys=["tool", "character-counter"],
            search_parents=True,
        ),
    ],
)

@app.command
def count(filename: Path, *, character="-"):
    print(filename.read_text().count(character))
```

### Integrating TOML Configuration with Cyclopts App

Source: https://github.com/brianpugh/cyclopts/blob/main/docs/source/user_classes.rst

Configures the Cyclopts App to read parameters from a TOML file, falling back to CLI arguments when values are not found in the configuration. `use_commands_as_keys=False` ensures parameters are not nested under command names.

```python
from cyclopts import App, Parameter, config
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Annotated

app = App(
   name="movie-maintainer",
   config=config.Toml("config.toml", use_commands_as_keys=False),
)

@Parameter(name="*")
@dataclass
class Config:
   user: str
   server: str = "media.sqlite"

@dataclass
class Movie:
   title: str
   year: int

@app.command
def add(movie: Movie, *, config: Config):
   print(f"Config: {config}")
   print(f"Adding movie: {movie}")

app()
```
